title: Cypress Community Clinic onramp scratchpad
content:
Context: Quick internal notes after kickoff with Cypress Community Clinic (regional non-profit network, 6 clinics, 3 EHR instances). They’re evaluating a private/on-prem Redwood deployment for a triage assistant (patient intake + basic triage, referrals). Primary concern: PHI compliance + minimal external egress. Secondary: cost predictability and 200ms token latency target for short messages.

Call summary (2026-02-18, 11:00am PST):
- Attendees: Dr. Renee Park (CMO), Jonah Keene (IT mgr), Maya S. (clinic ops), Alina T. (Redwood SE), Ethan B. (Redwood eng lead).
- Scope they asked: prototype assistant to handle new patient intake (demographics, chief complaint, meds, allergies), classify urgency (low/med/high), and surface suggested next steps for staff. Not replacing clinician decisions.
- Data flow requirement: clinic wants all PHI to stay within their VPC / air-gapped VM. Only metadata (deployment heartbeats, anonymized usage stats) may go to Redwood if customer opt-in.
- SLA asks: weekday business-hours 99.9% availability for UI-facing assistant. Latency: p95 < 500ms, target <200ms for short prompts (<150 tokens). Batch inference tolerable for backfill tasks (batch embeddings).
- Security: Must integrate with their KMS (AWS KMS) and support HSM-backed keys for secrets. Audit logs retained 7 years (compliance).

Immediate technical constraints / gotchas:
- EHR connectors: Cypress uses two older EHR exports (one HL7 v2 feed via local interface engine, one SQL Server reporting DB). Jonah insists on no direct writes back to EHR from our agent at MVP — only handoff to staff via task queue.
- Airgap: one clinic (rural) runs on isolated network with intermittent connectivity. On-prem package needs robust retry/queue behavior and local model variant that can run on a single A10 GPU node.
- Model pick: they like small context budget for faster latency. Recommend a distilled open model quantized to int8 + Redwood runtime optimizations. Evaluate 13B q4 variants for latency/cost tradeoff.
- KV cache: Most intake flows will have short session lengths but repeated patient follow-ups may benefit from ephemeral caching bound to session TTL=15m. Avoid persistent PHI in cache unless encrypted with customer KMS.
- Token quotas: Jonah wants token budget estimates for 3 months. Rough calc: 6 clinics * 120 intakes/day * avg 300 tokens/request ~ 648k tokens/day -> ~19M tokens/month. Need pricing estimate for private license + compute.

Open questions for customer follow-up:
1) Confirm whether telemetry can be sent as anonymized aggregates. Provide telemetry opt-in/out UI for their security team.
2) Exact list of fields from EHR extracts they can share for prototype (we requested a minimal CSV with demographics + encounter reason + provider id).
3) Which KMS/HSM provider: they said AWS KMS for onboarding but interested in future Thales HSM. Need to validate Redwood Private supports their HSM model.
4) Backup and restore SLA expectations for on-prem VMs. Who owns snapshot cadence? Cypress IT suggests nightly backups and 30-day retention.
5) Legal: need BAAs and executed DPA. Sales to coordinate legal touchpoint.

Next steps (internal):
- Alina: produce a short POC plan (2-week) that runs in their staging environment. POC goals: intake flow, urgency classifier, staff handoff queue, telemetry toggle. Deliverable: demo + runbook. ETA: draft plan 2026-02-24.
- Ethan: size compute for single-node offline model (target A10 baseline) + costs for 3 node HA vs single node with fallback to hosted for non-PHI. Deliverable: sizing doc + cost delta. ETA: 2026-02-26.
- Sales: start DPA/BAA thread. Attach standard private-deploy contract addendum.
- Solutions: prep a runbook snippet showing how to configure KMS integration and how Redwood encrypts caches in transit/at rest. Include sample IAM roles.
- Jonah: provide sample anonymized CSV of 200 historical intakes (remove MRN).

POC success criteria (for alignment):
- Automated intake completes 70% of fields accurately (based on staff verification sample of 100 intakes).
- Urgency classifier precision > 85% on high-urgency cases (recall also important).
- End-to-end UI latency p95 < 500ms in their staging network.
- No PHI egress outside VPC.

Riskiest assumptions:
- That a quantized 13B will meet latency targets on their available GPU. If not, fallback options: 1) smaller model for triage only, 2) hybrid routing: short latency path in-clinic, longer detailed summarization to a scheduled background job.
- That the clinic’s ops team can sanitize sample data quickly enough for POC. Delay here blocks classifier tuning.

Notes and prompts to prep for next customer call:
- Bring a short diagram contrasting fully air-gapped on-prem (no telemetry) vs limited-telemetry hybrid (anonymized metrics). Visual helps security team.
- Prepare simple explanation of KMS envelope encryption and how Redwood stores cache keys (we propose customer-managed keys with CMK ARN).
- Prepare cost estimate with three tiers: single-node local (metal) + Redwood private license; 3-node HA local; hybrid local + hosted fallback (non-PHI only) to reduce peak infra.
- Demo scripts: 8–10 example intakes including edge cases (multiple meds, free-text chief complaint abbreviations, non-English short phrases).

Random quick thoughts:
- Could offer a prebuilt HL7->CSV shim for them as a professional service if their interface engine is brittle.
- For rural clinic offline mode, consider a tiny LLM (2–3B) for minimal triage + cached templates to keep latency low when disconnected.

Slack refs / tickets to create:
- SE-EVAL: create eval set and metrics dashboard for Cypress POC (owner Alina).
- INF-OPS: confirm airgap install checklist (owner Ethan).
- SALES-LEGAL: start DPA thread with Cypress legal (owner Sales).

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after receiving sample CSV and Jonah’s confirmation on KMS ARN.
